For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the tahini came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

## What counts as tahini

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers tahini, as sold (188 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/potorti2026-tahini-quality-safety-inorganic-elements|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Potortì AG, Albergamo A, Nava V, Lo Turco V, Litrenta F, Spanò IM, Di Bella G · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/potorti2026-tahini-quality-safety-inorganic-elements">Chemical Composition and Nutritional Quality of Commercial Tahini</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/potorti2026-tahini-quality-safety-inorganic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/sadeghi2021-tahini-heavy-metals-voltammetry|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sadeghi, Naficeh, Behzadi, Hassan Rezaei, Behzad, Masoomeh, Jannat, Behrooz, Hajimahmoodi, Mannan · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sadeghi2021-tahini-heavy-metals-voltammetry">Simultaneous determination of heavy metals in Tahini by anodic stripping voltammetry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Human, Health and Halal Metrics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sadeghi2021-tahini-heavy-metals-voltammetry">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-tahini" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-tahini-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of tahini, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Tahini, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤10</td><td>≤10</td><td>≤10</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤10</td><td>≤10</td><td>≤10</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>3 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>3</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for tahini, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for tahini, as sold on this basis in the completed tahini ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:tahini-628f54cbb210:08c5ec54365a</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><div hidden data-form-reasons><p data-reason="no_numeric_value_or_bound" data-title="Spread or extreme value only">The source reports only a percentile, range or maximum for these samples, with no mean or median to place against the reference. ## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>

<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

In one study, lead across 31 groups of tahini ranged from 0.01 µg/kg (plain tahini product 15 (Tehran market)) to 0.48 µg/kg (plain tahini product 4 (Tehran market)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/sadeghi2021-tahini-heavy-metals-voltammetry|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sadeghi, Naficeh, Behzadi, Hassan Rezaei, Behzad, Masoomeh, Jannat, Behrooz, Hajimahmoodi, Mannan · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sadeghi2021-tahini-heavy-metals-voltammetry">Simultaneous determination of heavy metals in Tahini by anodic stripping voltammetry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Human, Health and Halal Metrics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sadeghi2021-tahini-heavy-metals-voltammetry">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, cadmium across 4 groups of tahini ranged from 10 µg/kg (T-2, Israel, toasted hulled) to 350 µg/kg (T-1, Turkey, organic hulled); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/potorti2026-tahini-quality-safety-inorganic-elements|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Potortì AG, Albergamo A, Nava V, Lo Turco V, Litrenta F, Spanò IM, Di Bella G · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/potorti2026-tahini-quality-safety-inorganic-elements">Chemical Composition and Nutritional Quality of Commercial Tahini</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/potorti2026-tahini-quality-safety-inorganic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>
